content:
Dossier


„

Kast wird in den nächsten Jahren regieren, und wir dürfen keine Angriffe, keine Sozialkürzungen, keine Prekarisierung der Arbeitsverhältnisse zulassen. Er ist ein bekennender Pinochetist, das Symbol der patriarchalischen und konservativen Reaktion. Wir laden euch ein, den Widerstand an euren Arbeits- und Studienplätzen zu organisieren. Als Arbeiter*innen und Student*innen, Frauen und Dissident*innen, Mapuche und Migrant*innen müssen wir uns zusammenschließen, uns in Verbänden, sozialen Vereinen, Studentenwerken, Gewerkschaften, Nachbarschaftsvereinigungen, Versammlungen und auf der Straße organisieren, um der extremen Rechten entgegenzutreten. Wir dürfen ihnen keinen Raum lassen

…“ Aus der span. Erklärung der Gruppierungen VENCER, La Red de Trabajadorxs Precarizadxs und Pan y Rosas vom 14.12.2025

dokumentiert in La Izquierda Diario


 (maschinenübersetzt), siehe

das Dossier zur Vorgeschichte der Wahl samt Infos über die Person Kast

 und hier die nachfolgende Entwicklung:


Chile: Zurück zum Neoliberalismus der 80er. Der Senat beschließt in einer »Mega-Reform« Steuergeschenke für Reiche, der Arbeitsminister wirbt für die 52-Stunden-Woche


„

Nach mehrstündiger Debatte hat der chilenische Senat am Donnerstag morgen um drei Uhr Ortszeit die sogenannte Mega-Reform der Regierung von José Antonio Kast beschlossen – mit 26 Ja- und 23 Nein-Stimmen bei einer Enthaltung. Rund vierzig Maßnahmen umfasst das Paket. Es sieht unter anderem die Senkung der Unternehmenssteuer von 27 auf 23 Prozent und Zahlungen an Unternehmen vor, deren Projekte aus Umweltgründen aufgegeben werden mussten. Kritik an dem Projekt kam nicht nur aus der Opposition, sondern auch vom Internationalen Währungsfonds. Der warnte vor Risiken bei den Steuereinnahmen, gerade weil keine Gegenfinanzierung für die »Mega-Reform« vorgesehen ist. Auch in der Bevölkerung glaubt einer Umfrage zufolge eine Mehrheit von 49 Prozent, dass das Vorhaben vor allem große Unternehmen und hohe Einkommen begünstigt. Nur 35 Prozent gehen demnach von positiven Effekten für die Beschäftigung aus. (…)


Der Politologe Gilberto Aranda kommentierte die Reformen der rechten Regierung so: Was Chile bisher hatte, war ein »durch Subventionen und andere Elemente abgemilderter Neoliberalismus. (…)


Nun konzentrieren sich die Bemühungen des Präsidenten im wesentlichen auf die Vertiefung und eine Rückkehr zu jenem orthodoxen neoliberalen Modell der späten 70er und frühen 80er Jahre.« Parallel dazu bereitet Arbeitsminister Tomás Rau eine Änderung der erst 2023 beschlossenen 40-Stunden-Woche vor und beruft sich dafür auf die Empfehlung einer eigens durch die Regierung eingesetzten Kommission, der Arbeitsgruppe zur Reaktivierung des Arbeitsmarktes. Die Wochenarbeitszeit soll in Zeiten hoher Nachfrage für Arbeiter und Angestellte auf 52 Stunden erhöht werden. Die Berechnung der Wochenarbeitszeit soll nicht mehr auf Basis von vier, sondern von 15 Wochen oder sogar auf das ganze Jahr berechnet werden. Schon heute zählt Chile unter den OECD-Staaten zu denen mit den höchsten Arbeitszeiten und der größten Ungleichheit. (…)


Doch auch der zentrale Gewerkschaftsverband CUT warnt davor, Arbeitsrechte weiter zu beschneiden und die 40-Stunden-Woche in Frage zu stellen. Erst 2023 hatte Chile die 40-Stunden-Woche eingeführt – als drittes Land in Lateinamerika überhaupt. Kritik äußerte CUT vor allem daran, dass die Erhöhung der Arbeitszeit nicht mehr als Überstunden vom Unternehmen bezahlt werden würde. Statt dessen sollen die Überstunden in einer anderen Woche mit weniger Arbeitszeit verrechnet werden. Es könnte laut CUT sogar so weit kommen, dass die Kompensation dieser zusätzlichen Stunden gar nicht eintrifft, wenn das Arbeitsverhältnis vorher endet. Die Kosten für diese Flexibilität der Unternehmen trage am Ende der Arbeiter. »Während die Unternehmen die Möglichkeit erhalten, den Arbeitstag nach ihren Bedürfnissen zu gestalten, verlieren die Beschäftigten Einkommen, Zeit für ihre Familien und die Sicherheit in ihrem Alltag«, heißt es in einer Mitteilung der CUT. Neben Kommunisten lehnen auch sozialistische Abgeordnete und das linke Parteienbündnis Frente Amplio die Änderung des Arbeitsgesetzes ab. Im Wahlkampf hatte Präsident Kast noch versprochen, die 40-Stunden-Woche nicht verändern zu wollen…“


Artikel von Robert Kohl Parra in der jungen Welt vom 18. Juli 2026

title: Das (noch) staatliche Wasserversorgungsunternehmen  AySA: Wer will Argentiniens Wasser?
content:
Dossier


Die aktuelle Situation der Auseinandersetzung ums Wasser in Argentinien, nach dem forcierten Rückzug von Suez aus der Wasserversorgung von Buenos Aires. Ein interessanter persönlicher argentinischer Blog, der sowohl die Rolle der Kirchner-Regierung bei Privatisierungsprozessen untersucht, als auch die UNO-Gläubigkeit mancher Linker kritisiert: Schliesslich habe die UNO (zusammen mit der Weltbank) auf dem „Weltgipfel des Wassers“ 2000 in Den Haag verhindert, dass in die Abschlusserklärung das „Menschenrecht auf Wasser“ aufgenommen worden sei. Der (spanische) Kommentar „

AGUAS ARGENTINAS, EL BANCO MUNDIAL Y EL GOBIERNO PRIVATISTA DE KIRCHNER

“

 bei „La Giralda“ vom 24. September 2005 und mehr dazu:


Es droht die Umwandlung der „Agua y Saneamientos Argentinos“ (AySA) in eine Aktiengesellschaft – Gewerkschaften rufen zur Verteidigund des Rechts auf Wasser auf


„

ZUR VERTEIDIGUNG DES RECHTES AUF WASSER UND LAND


ZUR VERTEIDIGUNG DER NATIONALEN SOUVERÄNITÄT


Im Namen der CTA der Arbeitnehmer*innen und der Autonomen CTA rufen wir die Arbeitnehmer*innen unseres Landes sowie soziale, gewerkschaftliche und kommunale Organisationen dazu auf, das Recht auf Wasser und Land zu verteidigen und – letztendlich – unsere nationale Souveränität zu verteidigen.


Einerseits lehnen wir jede Initiative, die eine Privatisierung, Konzessionsvergabe oder Umwandlung der „Agua y Saneamientos Argentinos“ (AySA) in eine Aktiengesellschaft vorsieht, aufs Schärfste ab; andererseits verurteilen wir die Gesetzesänderungen, die den Schutz des Bodens, der natürlichen Ressourcen und der territorialen Souveränität unseres Landes schwächen.


Im Juli 2025 wurde die von der nationalen Exekutive erlassene Dringlichkeitsverordnung (DNU) Nr. 493/2025 in Kraft gesetzt, die die regulatorischen Rahmenbedingungen für die von AySA erbrachten öffentlichen Dienstleistungen im Bereich Trinkwasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung ändert und den Einstieg von privatem Kapital in das Unternehmen ermöglicht. Das DNU 493/2025 legt einen neuen Rechtsrahmen für die Erbringung der öffentlichen Trinkwasser- und Abwasserdienstleistungen im Versorgungsgebiet des Unternehmens AySA S.A. fest und wirkt sich damit auf die Bedingungen für den Zugang zu Trinkwasser und zur Abwasserentsorgung für 15 Millionen Menschen aus. Diese DNU stellt eine marktwirtschaftliche Logik über jene Logik, die Wasser als ein grundlegendes Menschenrecht versteht, das wiederum durch die Resolution 64/292 der Generalversammlung der Vereinten Nationen, zahlreiche internationale Verträge, Urteile des Obersten Gerichtshofs und die argentinische Verfassung anerkannt ist. Sie ermöglicht die Unterbrechung der Versorgung bei Zahlungsrückständen, lockert die Kontrollen der Wasserqualität ab und weicht damit von den von der WHO festgelegten Parametern ab, hebt die Verpflichtung zum Ausbau der Versorgung innerhalb des Versorgungsgebiets auf und führt monatliche Tarifanpassungen ein, um die Rentabilität der Versorgung zu gewährleisten.


Im Mai dieses Jahres hat die nationale Regierung mit dem Beschluss 704/2026 eine nationale und internationale öffentliche Ausschreibung durchgeführt und den Privatisierungsplan für AySA auf den Weg gebracht, der eine Konzession mit einer Laufzeit von 30 Jahren und einer Verlängerungsoption vorsieht. Man rechnet mit Einnahmen in Höhe von 500 Millionen US-Dollar, doch die sozialen Folgen werden 15 Millionen Menschen betreffen.


Andererseits wird der Senat die Debatte über das fälschlicherweise als „Gesetz zur Unantastbarkeit des Privateigentums“ bezeichnete Gesetz aufnehmen, bei dem es sich um nichts anderes als ein Gesetz zur Auslandsübertragung von Land handelt.


Beide Initiativen sind Teil desselben systematischen Plans: der Zerstörung des Staates und der Auslieferung der Gemeingüter, die er für sein Volk schützen sollte. Wasser, Land und strategische Ressourcen sind Gemeingüter, die für das Leben, die nationale Entwicklung und das Wohlergehen heutiger und künftiger Generationen unverzichtbar sind. Ihr Schutz darf nicht wirtschaftlichen oder spekulativen Interessen ohne nationale Bindung untergeordnet werden. (…)


Wir rufen euch dazu auf, weiterhin Ideen und Maßnahmen zu entwickeln, um unsere Gemeingüter zu verteidigen und erneut zu bekräftigen, dass Wasser und Land keine Handelsware sind und dass die nationale Souveränität nicht verhandelbar ist.

author: anonerror
title: La llama, siempre viva, de la Revolución Social
content:
Foto: Archivo Fotográfico Guerra Civil Española - Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo (CNT)

Este domingo, 19 de julio, se conmemora en muchos puntos de la geografía española el 90 aniversario de la Revolución Social. No se recuerda solo en España. La efeméride también se celebra en distintos países como Argentina, Francia, Italia, Chile, Grecia o Suecia, entre otros. En decenas de ciudades se han organizado charlas, exposiciones, seminarios de estudios, exhibiciones de películas producidas durante la Guerra Civil… Estas celebraciones pretenden rendir homenaje a lo que el movimiento anarquista internacional, pero no solo, recuerda como uno de los procesos revolucionarios más singulares del siglo XX: la Revolución Española.

¿Pero de qué revolución hablamos? Hablamos del proceso de transformación social acelerado que tuvo lugar en España a partir del 19 de julio de 1936, más concretamente en aquellas zonas del territorio español no controladas por Franco tras el alzamiento militar. Un proceso revolucionario en el que el movimiento libertario tuvo un papel destacado y para el que los anarquistas se habían estado preparando durante décadas.

Y es que, si hablamos de la presencia del anarquismo en el Estado español, tenemos que pensar que las organizaciones locales de inspiración ácrata vinculadas al movimiento obrero internacional, tuvieron una implantación considerable desde el último tercio del siglo XIX. A partir de ahí, ni los procesos de criminalización orquestados por el Estado, ni la pugna ideológica con los sectores marxistas, ni la conflictividad interna del propio movimiento, lograron que la cultura política anarquista dejara de tener cierta prevalencia en el seno del movimiento obrero español. Una cultura política, la libertaria, que ponía en el centro de su programa político la preparación para la revolución, ya no solo fomentando la autocapacitación cultural, ideológica y militante de cada trabajador o trabajadora afín, sino prefigurando el mundo del mañana a través de la paulatina consolidación de una institucionalidad autónoma que no solo pasaba por la conformación de sociedades obreras, sino que también tenía que ver con la urdimbre de ateneos, escuelas racionalistas, periódicos, editoriales o grupos naturistas, por citar solo algunos ejemplos, que insuflaban vida a ese mundo propio.

En todo caso, y para entender todo lo que ocurrió a partir de julio de 1936, la creación de la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT), ya en 1910, supuso un hito de consideración que explica cómo la articulación del anarquismo español en torno a una organización de masas, en este caso de carácter sindical, posibilitó que el movimiento libertario, paulatinamente minorizado a nivel internacional en el primer tercio del siglo XX, siguiera teniendo una implantación considerable en el seno del movimiento obrero español. Una pujanza que, en el plano interno, se vio asegurada por la toma de acuerdos que reforzaron el músculo sindical de la organización —como la creación de los Sindicatos Únicos (1918-1919)— y también se vio favorecida por el prestigio alcanzado por la organización anarcosindicalista tras el triunfo de la huelga de La Canadiense, que posibilitó la aprobación de la jornada laboral de 8 horas en el marco del Estado español.

Sin embargo, el crecimiento de la CNT y la proliferación de un movimiento obrero no sometido a directrices partidistas, autónomo y revolucionario, no fueron bien recibidos por el Estado y la patronal, quienes primero intentaron amedrentar a la militancia cenetista con la violencia terrorista ejercida por las bandas de pistoleros del Sindicato Libre (una violencia que, entre decenas de sindicalistas asesinados, se llevó por delante a dos secretarios generales de la CNT: Evelio Boal y Salvador Seguí), y luego, tras la llegada al poder de Miguel Primo de Rivera por la vía dictatorial, consiguieron la ilegalización del sindicato anarquista y el paso a la clandestinidad y exilio de buena parte de sus militantes más destacados.

Tras más de ocho años de régimen dictatorial encabezado, primero, por Miguel Primo de Rivera, y luego por Dámaso Berenguer, la llegada de la II República (1931) fue saludada con esperanza por buena parte de los sectores populares, ansiosos de un cambio de régimen que ampliara las libertades políticas e hiciera frente a las desigualdades sociales. Sin embargo, la “república de trabajadores”, tal y como rezaba el artículo 1 de la Constitución republicana, demostró muy pronto su …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Nearly 1,000 Wildfires in Canada Continue to Burn as Trump & Carney Double Down on Fossil Fuels
content:
Millions of people across North America have experienced hazardous air pollution this month as nearly a thousand active wildfires continue to rage in Canada. In addition to releasing hazardous chemicals and smoke darkening skies across the continent, the fires in Canada have also disproportionately impacted Indigenous communities, forcing thousands to evacuate their homes. Republican politicians have been loath to acknowledge the role of the climate crisis in making extreme weather events like this more frequent and intense, instead blaming Canadian officials for poor forest management. President Donald Trump has even threatened to impose new tariffs on Canada over the record levels of hazardous air.


Independent Canadian journalist Rachel Gilmore says that while Trump’s comments are “extremely offensive” to people in the country, Liberal Prime Minister Mark Carney’s policies — while acknowledging the science — also do little to mitigate the climate crisis as he approves new oil pipelines that would operate for decades.


“He’s not exactly taking the climate action that we need here in Canada,” Gilmore says of Carney.

ICE

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Justice for Lorenzo": Houston Community Demands Accountability After ICE Killing of Mexican Father
content:
Houston community members continue to demand justice for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the 52-year-old Mexican father who was shot and killed by an

ICE

 agent July 7. He had lived in the United States for nearly 35 years and had three U.S. citizen children. The

ICE

 agents involved in his killing have not been identified, and it’s unclear whether they remain on active duty.


For more on the community response, we get a report from

Democracy Now!

 producers on the ground in Houston. To many people in the city’s immigrant communities, Salgado Araujo was “Houston’s dad,” representative of their own families and not a dangerous criminal as the government has tried to portray him.


“He looks just like all of our parents. He has the same story, the same American dream,” a resident named Sonia told

Democracy Now!


“We are demanding justice for Lorenzo, but it’s not just that,” a mourner said at a rally. “These terrorists coming from the government, it’s not just in Houston, it’s not just in Texas, it’s not just in the United States. It’s terrorism all over the world.”

title: U.S. Escalates War on Iran, Targeting Civilian Infrastructure as 3 U.S. Soldiers Are Killed
content:
The United States is expanding its attacks on Iran after three U.S. soldiers were killed over the weekend, the first U.S. fatalities in the conflict since March. Two U.S. service members were killed in an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan, and a third soldier was killed in northern Iraq during a “controlled detonation” of a downed Iranian drone. The United States has now bombed Iran for nine consecutive nights, and Iran has retaliated by striking U.S. allies across the Persian Gulf. The war, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has squeezed global supplies of oil and gas.


“The United States has considerable violence at its disposal, but it has limited political capacity to dictate terms,” says Toby Jones, associate professor of Middle East history at Rutgers University. Jones says that while the United States has tried to “inflict pain” on Iranian civilians in order to weaken the government, “it’s hard to say that it’s working.”

author: TGEU
title: UK Government’s final Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance fails to protect trans, non-binary and intersex children and young people
content:
Eight civil society organisations express serious concern following the UK Government’s publication of the final 2026

Keeping Children Safe in Education

 guidance, which will come into force in England on 1 September 2026.


Last week, on 7 July 2026, the UK Government released the final 2026

Keeping Children Safe in Education

 statutory guidance for schools

 and colleges in England, and made it come into force in England on 1 September 2026. Earlier this year,

IGLYO and TGEU warned that the draft guidance raised serious legal, safeguarding, and human rights concerns

. We highlighted that it risked undermining equality law, data protection obligations, confidentiality, dignity, non-discrimination, and equal access to safe and inclusive education.

Sadly, the final guidance retains most of these core concerns.


We recognise the importance of safeguarding guidance that supports schools and colleges to protect all children from harm. We also recognise the responsibility of governments to provide clarity to educators, families, and young people. However, the final KCSIE guidance does not meet this responsibility when it comes to trans, non-binary, and intersex children and young people.


We, as civil society, remain committed to constructive dialogue with the UK Government, and want to work towards schools that are safe, supportive, and rights-based for every child. However, meaningful dialogue must lead to meaningful protection. The publication of this guidance is another deeply worrying indication that the UK Government is failing to protect trans, non-binary, and intersex children and young people. Worse, it puts them in harm’s way.


The guidance continues to treat children’s gender identity and social transition primarily through a safeguarding lens. This framing is wrong and harmful and positions trans, non-binary and intersex children as ‘risks’ rather than as rights holders. Being trans, non-binary or intersex is not, in itself, a safeguarding concern. Safeguarding should protect children from violence, bullying, discrimination, abuse, neglect and exclusion. It should not be used to justify policies that isolate children, undermine their dignity, or make them afraid to seek support from trusted adults.


We are particularly concerned that the guidance places significant barriers in the way of children who request support related to social transition, including around presentation, pronouns use, access to facilities, accommodation, and participation in school life. The guidance also relies on rigid and binary understandings of “sex” that risk harming trans, non-binary and intersex children and young people, including those whose bodies, identities or lived experiences do not fit narrow sex-based categories.


The guidance states that schools must not allow pupils into toilets, changing rooms, or boarding or residential accommodation designated for the “opposite sex”, with no exceptions, and applies similarly restrictive language to sports segregated by sex. These provisions exclude trans, non-binary and intersex children and young people from ordinary school life. They may force young people into separate or stigmatising arrangements, restrict their participation in education, sport and residential activities, and increase their exposure to bullying, humiliation, and social isolation.


Organisations working directly with young people in England have raised the everyday harms caused by restrictive school policies, including young people avoiding toilets at school because they do not feel safe or able to use them. These are not abstract policy disagreements. They are immediate risks to children’s health, wellbeing, dignity, and education.


We are also deeply concerned about confidentiality and data protection. The guidance strongly encourages parental involvement when a child asks for support with social transition, while failing to provide sufficient safeguards to ensure that any information-sharing is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and in the best interests of the child. Some trans, non-binary and intersex children and young people face rejection, hostility, abuse or homelessness when sensitive information about their identity, sex characteristics or personal circumstances is disclosed without their consent, including to their caregivers. Any decision to share such information must be made on a careful, case-by-case basis, taking into account the child’s wishes, age, maturity, safety and home …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: ‘We’re the Canary in the Coal Mine’: Palestine Action Activists Sentenced As ‘Terrorists’ Speak Out
content:
“They’re saying it’s so that I won’t radicalise anyone else, which is a bullshit excuse to alienate us from the world.” 


This is Ellie Kamio speaking – a 30-year-old former nursery teacher and one of four Palestine Action activists sentenced as terrorists last month over a break-in at an Israeli-owned arms factory in 2024. 


Ellie and one of her fellow defendants, Charlotte ‘Lottie’ Head, 29, spoke to Novara Media about what prison is like after being sentenced with a ‘terrorist connection’, despite not being convicted of a terror offence. 


Ellie and Lottie are now subject to an

enhanced contact vetting (ECV) scheme

 for “terrorist prisoners”, meaning their contact with the outside world is restricted to a maximum of 20 people, who all have to undergo vetting. Only these 20 people can call, email, write to or visit them. Ellie and Lottie spoke to Novara Media via one of their registered contacts.


Lottie, previously a charity worker supporting victims of domestic violence, called it a “further attempt to break and psychologically punish us” through isolation, and a move “to reduce our world yet further”. 


Both women already spent 18 months in prison before their first trial – far beyond the standard legal custody time limit for unconvicted defendants of six months. In May they were found guilty of criminal damage for smashing up property, including military drones, at an Elbit Systems site in Filton, Gloucestershire. 


Lottie stressed that the ECV vetting process can be intimidating for friends and family to go through, particularly due to fears around the potential impact on immigration status, work or simply “the worry of being caught in the crosshairs of the oppression we are experiencing”. 


Ellie’s mum Emma Kamio told Novara Media that the ECV has led to some tough decisions – like Ellie deciding to drop her younger sister Sadie as one of her 20 contacts, because Sadie finds visiting prison too traumatic to do regularly. Now, Ellie can’t even speak to her sister on the phone. 


Emma – a Swansea-based small business owner

who was “traumatised” by her own brush with counterterrorism police

 in connection to Ellie’s case – added that there’s additional “pressure” on the 20 chosen contacts. “People are going to get tired,” she said, and life happens: they might go travelling, not be able to visit or not be available for phone calls. It becomes a real commitment, not for fair-weather friends. 


Prison in a heatwave.


The word Ellie uses to describe prison is “neglect”. “I wouldn’t say ‘neglectful’ because it’s not only a place that neglects people, but also a place where neglected people go.” 


Both Ellie and Lottie are currently incarcerated in HMP Bronzefield, on the outskirts of Ashford in Surrey. Inside, Ellie said, inmates are “dehumanised daily, multiple times a day” and “treated like dangerous animals, not human beings”. Examples are a recent dinner of a “plain jacket potato in a cup” and how “staff or officers will talk about you when you’re standing right there”. 


On the issue of food, Emma said her daughter’s budget is mostly used in the canteen [prison shop], supplementing sub-par prison meals with vitamins and extras like nuts (Ellie is a vegetarian). Emma pointed out the irony of Bronzefield’s private owner, Sodexo, also being a food services and catering company. 


Following soaring temperatures in June, Lottie said: “Prison in a heatwave is hell on earth. 

In Bronzefield, you cannot open the windows in your cell. This means that, with prisoners locked up for the vast majority of the day, there is no fresh air or way of dispelling heat from the cells.


“It truly highlights how staff see prisoners as ‘other’, sometimes even subhuman.” 


When temperatures reached 34C in the south east at the end of June, Lottie said “our entire wing didn’t even have the paltry fans each cell is supposed to be furnished with” and prisoners were “forbidden from wearing shorts more than one inch above the knee or vests with thin straps”. The UK has since experienced another, longer heatwave this month. 


A spokesperson for HMP Bronzefield encouraged prisoners to raise complaints directly with the prison and said: “We deny these allegations in full. Whilst we can’t comment on individuals, all prisoners are managed in line with the policies and procedures governing the entire UK prison estate.” 


Canaries in the coal mine.

author: Fozzie
title: Runaway Shop Comics - Take Care of Business (1973)
content:
A comic strip about the occupation of a workplace published in August 1973 by people associated with the post-Situationist group For Ourselves in California.

The PDF and the introduction below are taken from the Lust For Life site. (This site includes a huge amount of material, much of it worthwhile. However it is worth noting that the site's list of contents commences with several documents about the Rothschilds and includes nonsense such as "COVID-1984 as the Great [Rothschildian] Reset", alongside a typically wearying roll call of enduring conspiracy theory topics.)

Already in the early 1970s, when the intervention involving the subject comic book took place, the ruling class war on the working/middle class — with lots of ideological cover, religious, "conservative"-political, etc. — was well underway, often without that middle/working class realizing thet they were being targeted for dis-empowerment and impoverishment.

One manifestation of this war was the "runaway shop" phenomenon.

All over the rust belt, and throughout the U.S., corporations were shutting down industrial plants, laying off the the workers formally employed in those plants, destroying the workers' unions thereby, with the corporations often also reneging on their pension obligations to those workers, and, thereby, impoverishing or ghost-towning entire cities, while the corporations moved their industrial plant assets to "Third World" countires, where ruling class/CIA created/supported dictatorships prohibited unions, and held down wages, burgeoning the profits of the "runaway shop" corporations.

One of the non-member associates of FOR OURSELVES was employed by a "runaway shop" in the San Francisco Bay Area of Northern California, and enlisted two members of FOR OURSELVES to collaborate, with him, in producing an intervention among the workers of that runaway shop, whose closure was imminent. One of those FOR OURSELVES members had developed consumate skills in realistic illustration, and produced all of the images for the resulting "comic book". This "comic book" also featured new efforts by FOR OURSELVES members to express the fundamental theory of the Marxian critique of capitalism, including of state-capitalism, fascist and Stalinist alike, in language closer to typical English, such as this expression of the Marxian surplus-value theory of the capitalist ruling class's exploitation of the working class:

"What do you mean, they don't owe us anything? Do you think the owners built this plant and all these machines by themselves? Hell No! It was us, and other workers like us! The difference between what they pay us in wages and what they can get for what we produce they keep! And they use it to buy more workers like us and more machines, to keep more of that difference, and so it goes, man! Communist, Sheeeit! They do it to you the same way all over the world — Russia and China too!".

This comic book advocated, to the worker's of this particular runaway shop — somewhat recklessly, considering the sanctions that the ruling class controlled police forces might have visited upon their heads as a consequence — that they occupy the plant, and hold its assets hostage so as to extract severance package and pension benefits from its owners. The non-member associate of FOR OURSELVES who had originally catalyzed this intervention distributed the "comic book" among his co-workers, and those co-workers chose not to implement the occupation that the "comic book" advocated.

They did so, probably, in many cases, out of fear, and out of habitual subservience, but also, in many cases, out of a sober assessment of the relationship of their potential forces to those of the repressive state that such an action would have brought down upon them, and out of a realistic, likely cost-versus-benefits analysis for such an action.

A clear formulation of the constitution, institutions, and socio-political processes of societal self-reproduction of a higher successor social system to that of the present, [state-]capital/wage-labor social relation of social reproduction, is prerequisite to any successful movement for trans-capitalist social revolution today, and such a formulation was missing from this intervention. author: DOPE Magazine
title: The 1926 General Strike
content:
Article from DOPE Magazine issue 34 (Summer 2026). DOPE Magazine is a quarterly libertarian-socialist street newspaper. We print 40,000 per issue, our mainly homeless vendors sell the paper for £3 and keep 100% of the money. Support us: subscribe!  DOPE Magazine

One hundred years ago, two million workers joined Britain's largest-ever general strike. They faced up not just to their bosses and the government, but also their own union leaders. For over two weeks, this momentous event shook the very core of Britain.

In 1817, William Benbow, a self-educated shoemaker, was released from prison after participating in a failed insurrection. He looked to formulate a new revolutionary strategy, which he called the "Grand National Holiday".

He toured the country for years promoting his idea. Then, in 1842, Staffordshire miners initiated a strike. They demanded not just better pay, but also political representation. Eventually, 500,000 workers across the country would join them, before it was crushed through a combination of military repression and lowered food prices. The first General Strike on earth had been defeated.

Following this defeat, craft unions that excluded unskilled workers dominated. Rather than fighting their bosses, they often tried to work with them. They built large financial reserves, and soon trade unions were more likely to be led by top-hatted officials in London than Staffordshire miners. A new organisation for these bureaucrats to coordinate with each other was formed: the Trades Union Congress (TUC).

Unskilled workers continued to be pushed by their bosses to work faster, longer, and harder for less money. In the summer of 1888, unwilling to take it anymore, they erupted. Women working at the Bryant and May factory walked out against deadly conditions. They won, and were quickly succeeded by tram drivers, gas stokers, and dockers.

New general unions were formed, and over the next decade, union membership increased from 750,000 to 2 million. Whilst many top-hatted union officials remained, the rank-and-file of workers at the bottom countered them, organising unofficial strikes when their union leaders refused to endorse action.

They also agitated for a “Triple Alliance”: an agreement among the industrial unions to strike in support of one another. The union leaders, wanting to put their members back under their control, eventually formed such an alliance. Secretly, however, they hoped that its threat alone would prevent them from actually needing to follow through.

In 1921, the mine owners announced pay cuts to offset declining profits. Miners called on the Triple Alliance for help; however, on 15th April, the unions announced they would not call a strike in support of them. Deemed “Black Friday”, the miners were eventually forced to accept the cuts.

By 1925, mine owners, with the government's support, again proposed further cuts to miners’ wages. However, this time, the TUC, under pressure from its rank-and-file, remained steadfast in its decision to call out its members for a general strike against this. The government backed off and agreed to subsidise miners' wages for nine months. Workers celebrated, proclaiming it “Red Friday”. But for this government, this was no defeat: they were simply buying time.

The government spent the next year drafting a series of plans to deploy the military, police, and middle-class volunteers to break any future general strike. On the other side, union leaders did little. In fact, they were keen to avoid such a dispute altogether.

With the miners' subsidies soon to run out, the TUC began negotiations again with Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin. They begged for any sort of compromise. But this time the government was convinced to see their position through. The miners’ subsidies ended, and, refusing to work for lower wages, they were locked out of their pits.

Yet the TUC still refused to call a General Strike. Then, on 3rd May 1926, rank-and-file printworkers at The Daily Mail pulled the trigger. They refused to print an anti-union front page, and Baldwin cut off negotiations with the TUC, calling it an attack on free speech. The TUC was left with no option. The General Strike was finally on.

The TUC only called out certain industries to join the miners: railways, docks, printshops, drivers, and iron and steelworks. However, many workers in industries not officially called out by the TUC still walked out on that first day. They mobilised under the slogan “Not …

author: DOPE Magazine
title: One More Method Of Keeping Us In Line. One More Party Called Green This Time.
content:
Article from DOPE Magazine issue 34 (Summer 2026). DOPE Magazine is a quarterly libertarian-socialist street newspaper. We print 40,000 per issue, our mainly homeless vendors sell the paper for £3 and keep 100% of the money. Support us: subscribe!  DOPE Magazine

For the third time in a decade, the British left has found its saviour. First it was Corbyn. Then it was Corbyn again. Now it's Zack. He's got a rent control policy and a TikTok strategy!

The lefties have a new golden boy. Flanked by articulate mancunian plumber Hannah Spencer, Zack Polanski’s Greens have, within a very short time of his leadership election, gained control of 5 more councils, won a by-election and increased their membership to over 200,000. In some polls, the Greens have even overtaken Labour. Polanski is media-savvy, combative, and willing to argue back against reform. He talks about cost-of-living issues and relates this to inequality and climate change. The Greens now seem like a serious political force, capable of taking a significant number of seats in the next general election from the Labour and Reform voter base, rather than being seen by most of the country as hopeless middle-class tofu-eating do-gooders.

This song sounds familiar. Que the slow chant of “oooohhhh jjjeerremmmy Cccooorrrbbbyyynnn” to the theme of the white stripes seven nation army at every single music festival in 2017. But as we know, instead of the People's Republic of Islington North taking power, we had Keir Starmer cancelling the £28 billion green investment pledge, cutting benefits for disabled people, selling weapons for the Israelis to carry out genocide, and a resurgent far-right street movement which threatens, via Reform, to take power. But don’t worry, because this time it's different, this time, Zack Polanski is going to sort everything out.

Green Party politics, like Corbynism before it, has to pretend something that just isn’t true. That the state is a neutral instrument, that different political persuasions can pick and use as they would like. But this isn’t how the state works- its primary structural function is to maintain order for capitalism to continue to work. This matters for Polanski's greens because the institution he is trying to capture was not built for the purposes he wants to use it for, and will actively resist those purposes. What would have happened if Corbyn had actually won in 2017? In the weeks and months following a Corbyn government, in all likelihood, the pound would have tanked. This is because capital is mobile and answers to no electorate, and most importantly, knows how to send a message. The press would have gone into full overdrive, and the Bank of England Treasury would be in Corbyn's office, telling him exactly what the European Central Bank had told Alexis Tsipras and Syriza in 2015: moderate, or the money doesn’t work. And moderating means changing nothing; just like Syriza, who went on to enforce even more austerity, or Mitterand's government in France in 1981, which lasted 2 years before doing a complete U-turn.

Maybe Corbyn might have succeeded in passing some radical policies, not by getting his image right or managing the press better, but by having an organised movement outside of parliament capable of pushing his program through. For instance, unions ready to strike against the inevitable capital flight. Workers prepared to occupy workplaces to prevent closure. A street movement that would be ready to riot and control areas, making backing down more dangerous than pressing ahead- parliament being a ratification of something that was already happening in workplaces and the streets, rather than the thing itself.

This is what happened during Allende's socialist government in Chile: in response to factory owners leaving with all the investment, workers took over the factories and kept the government alive. Ultimately, a pact between the ITT Corporation, the CIA and Chile's military bombed the presidential palace, killed Allende, overthrew his government, and installed a fascist Junta. During Corbyn's time, a serving general reportedly said that the army would “take direct action” if Corbyn became prime minister, and MI5 ran files on Corbyn for decades. To see how this scenario might play out, it's worth watching the Channel 4 series “A Very British Coup”, in which a left-wing Labour leader is brought down by a coalition of MI5, newspaper magnates and the civil service. Whilst it's a work of fiction, the events …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Mamdani Looking Into Arresting Netanyahu If He Visits New York
content:
Zohran Mamdani’s team is exploring whether he can order the arrest of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu if he visits New York later this year.


Speaking to the New York Times, the mayor said there was “an active conversation” about whether his office has the authority to enforce a warrant issued by the international criminal court (ICC) in 2024.


Netanyahu is expected to travel to the city for the UN general assembly in September. 


“I believe that prime minister Netanyahu belongs in the Hague,” Mamdani said on an episode of the Times’s the Interview podcast on Saturday.


“He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the international criminal court, and what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these past many years.” 


He added: “Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that’s what we will do, but we won’t be writing our own laws to that end.”


The ICC warrant, issued amid Israel’s genocide in Gaza, describes Netanyahu as a co-conspirator in “the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare; and the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts.”  


Mamdani said while campaigning to be mayor last year that he would arrest the prime minister if he visited New York. Yet his decision after taking office to retain police commissioner Jessica Tisch, who oversaw a crackdown on pro-Palestine students, led to doubts over whether he would follow through on that pledge.


​Earlier in July, Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir cancelled a planned trip to New York after rights groups filed a criminal complaint against him with the Department of Justice.

author: Leituras CCLA
title: Camillo Berneri - Abolição e Extinção do Estado (1936)
content:
Neste texto incisivo, escrito em plena Guerra Civil Espanhola, o anarquista italiano Camillo Berneri desmonta a teoria marxista‑leninista da “extinção do Estado” e expõe suas contradições à luz da experiência concreta da Revolução Russa. Publicado em 1936 no jornal Guerra de Classe, em Barcelona, o artigo é uma crítica direta ao modelo bolchevique e uma defesa clara da perspectiva anarquista de abolição imediata do Estado através da revolução social e da organização federalista.


Berneri analisa a teoria de Engels e Lenin sobre o chamado “semi‑Estado proletário”, mostrando como a promessa de um Estado transitório que desapareceria naturalmente nunca se realizou. Para ele, a URSS não caminhava rumo à extinção do Estado, mas sim para um capitalismo de Estado cada vez mais centralizado, repressivo e burocrático. O autor demonstra como o partido bolchevique substituiu o proletariado real, instaurando uma nova classe dominante e destruindo qualquer possibilidade de autogestão.


O texto também revisita o programa original de 1917 — supressão da polícia, do exército permanente, da burocracia profissional, revogabilidade dos cargos, democracia soviética — e mostra como nenhum desses pontos foi cumprido. Em vez disso, Berneri descreve a ascensão de uma oligarquia partidária, marcada por expurgos, perseguições internas e concentração absoluta de poder no Comitê Central. Para ele, o stalinismo não é um desvio, mas a consequência lógica do “ditatorialismo leninista”.


Ao final, Berneri afirma que a fórmula “ditadura do proletariado” é tão enganosa quanto o “povo soberano” do jacobinismo: ambas abrem caminho para o autoritarismo e para o surgimento de novos Bonapartes. Seu texto é, ao mesmo tempo, uma crítica histórica e um alerta político — defendendo que a revolução social só pode florescer através da autonomia, da autogestão e da abolição imediata do Estado, e não por meio de sua conquista.


Vídeo realizado pelo Centro de Cultura Libertária da Amazônia - CCLA (Belém do Pará, Brasil) - 2025.

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: The Red-Brown Paradox: National Syndicalism within the Modern Far-Left
content:
In one of my previous articles, I stated that “if earlier forms of fascism emerged from currents within the left, could a new left‑originating variant appear again? Preventing future left‑wing expressions of fascism requires beginning with a precise, grounded understanding of what fascism actually is, since genuine anti‑fascism depends on that clarity”.

Pierre Tru-Dank, also known as Joshua E. Masters, was a once-contributor of “leftypol”, that sponsored a Richard Wolff lecture at the Judson Memorial Church Assembly Hall, with Wolff referring to the community as an "interesting group of people”.
 
He recently translated a book of Edouard Berth “The Misdeeds of the Intellectuals” (French: Les méfaits des intellectuels). Here, Edouard Berth is a theorist of French syndicalism and disciple of Georges Sorel who co-founded the Cercle Proudhon, a group that gave birth to syncretic and proto-fascist revisionist Marxist ideology called “national syndicalism”.
 
Pierre Tru-Dank is being displayed as a left-wing content creator by Leftypedia, an online English language socialist encyclopedia dedicated to providing a coherent platform about leftist politics hosted on Miraheze. His name appears as a left-wing content creator in IWW (Industrial Workers of the World) subreddits and some other socialist subreddits such as socialism. In those reddit communities, he is mostly considered as a Marxist-De Leonist.
 
On Feb 21st of this year, Pierre Tru Dank released an article entitled “An Outline of Socialist Industrial Unionism for the 21st Century”, in which he co-authored with Shandon Simpson, otherwise known as “Zoran Zoltanous”, publishing articles on the “The Fascio Newsletter”. In the article, they highly quoted the American Marxist Daniel De Leon who developed Socialist Industrial Unionism, Georges Sorel, Proudhon, Karl Marx, and Friedrich Engels. It would be a bit strange for those who are not familiar with their contents but it’s normal for the proto-fascist national syndicalists, classical fascists and national Bolsheviks to quote the national syndicalist thinkers such as Edouard Berth, Georges Valois, Hubert Lagardelle, and Georges Sorel along with National Bolsheviks thinkers such as Karl Otto Paetel and Ernst Niekisch in addition to prominent socialist thinkers such as Proudhon, Karl Marx, and Friedrich Engels.
 
Also, it’s to note that Pierre Tru-Dank was once a member of American Communist Party (ACP), the MAGA Marxist-Leninist party with founder like Jackson Hinkle and Haz Al-Din who are inspired by Aleksandr Dugin, the philosopher of Fourth Political Theory. However, Pierre Tru-Dank resigned from ACP voluntarily in November 2025. Currently, he is known to have founded a syndicalist organisation in Canada called “Canadian Syndicalist Federation”.
  
Given the fact that Sorelian (revisionist) Marxism—which merged revolutionary syndicalism with nationalism and helped give rise to proto-fascist national syndicalism and fascism, combating fascism effectively requires a strong ideological counterforce. Since historically, all forms of fascism have rejected liberal principles like democracy, open migration, individualism, limited government, and civil rights, a key strategy could involve championing these liberal values. A more radical approach might involve advocating for international solidarity beyond the identity politics in the light of social justice, stateless solutions to intersectional oppressions, acknowledging the uniqueness of the individuals, the recognition of class struggle as a driving force of the history and defending universal human rights along with the civil liberties of every human being.

author: Simon Childs
title: What Do the World Cup Final and Andy Burnham Have in Common?
content:
With the football done and dusted at least until the domestic season starts in about five minutes time, we have the small matter of the sixth new prime minister in a decade starting his new role in earnest today.


Spain emerged deserving winners after a tense game went to extra time, finally unlocking the Argentinian defence in the 106th minute when substitute Ferran Torres seized on a header back into the box and thumped the ball past Emi Martínez.


Football may not have been the winner after a forgettable match, but Argentina were certainly the losers, underscored by Leandro Paredes

who appeared to start a fight

 with a Spain player after the final whistle.


The event was a victory for the creeping American-style injection of advertising opportunities and candy floss into every spare moment and orifice – and also into some moments

that were never spare

 – at the expense of whatever sporting integrity remains.


Take half-time, which was lengthened especially to include a show which involved a smirking Ronaldo and Ronaldinho driving Madonna around in a Mad Max-style buggy and the Muppets and Coldplay covering The White Stripes’ Seven Nation Army. It’s not exactly that it wasn’t entertaining, but by the time Ted Lasso was introducing Justin Bieber I had slightly forgotten about the quite important sport thingy I had tuned in for.


Perhaps even more bizarre was the pre-match ceremony, in which the World Cup trophy was presented in a special Louis Vuitton case before Tom Cruise gave a speech about how football unites nations as the Argentina players wondered when they could get their Malvinas banner out again and Donald Trump glowered on like Mr Burns.


After watching Fifa president Gianni Infantino palling around with Trump on the winners’ podium, it will be nice to return to the calm and incorruptible world of UK politics and the cosy familiarity of a new prime minister.


Today, Andy Burnham will give his first speech as PM, completing his bloodless coup. He’s expected to say that he must deliver “tangible” improvements and give people “more breathing room” on the cost of living. He’ll also be hoping for some breathing room of his own. Making a real impact before the next election will be a tough ask, leading some commentators to observe that his success may depend on

vibes more than results

.


So far the vibes are mixed. On the one hand, he’s scrapping plans for mandatory digital ID cards – perhaps the most out-of-touch of Starmer’s policies – and the money will go towards helping with the cost of living. On the other hand, Shabana Mahmood looks likely to become chancellor ahead of Ed Miliband. 


While Miliband is the soft-left choice, believed to have the vision to drive change, Mahmood “is very much on the right of the party. She was one of the biggest supporters of cutting welfare”, according to one MP quoted in the Independent,

which also reports

 she was a major internal critic of Rachel Reeves for policies such as putting VAT on private schools.


Thames Water is set to be

put into “special administration”

 in a signal that privatisers’ days of piss-taking might be drawing to a close. But before you allow yourself too much hope, Burnham is also expected to announce

new oil and gas drilling licences

 in the North Sea,

drawing praise

 from Trump.


What are we to make of this mixed picture? Perhaps there’s an analogy to be drawn with the football. After England had an epic choking fit against Argentina, a debate broke out: initially manager Thomas Tuchel copped all of the criticism for his substitutions. Then, the football punditry take-machine spat out a second line of argument, which was that Tuchel’s decisions handing Argentina the initiative were merely a symptom of a deeper malaise in the English game.


Is Burnham the master operator who will turn things around? Is it possible, as Times political commentator

Patrick Maguire has argued

, that the missing ingredient for the UK’s last few PMs has been leadership? And does it follow therefore that Burnham could do some good were he to actually lead? Or was the ideological void that was the Starmer project a mere symptom of a political party and system of which Burnham is surely a part – one that is denuded of ideas and the will to make change at a systemic level?


Today Burnham will try to articulate a coherent vision to the country. Is this a new dawn, or Starmerism 2.0? We’re about to find out.

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Trumps Iran-Dilemma – Warum die Straße von Hormuz geschlossen und der Sprit teuer bleiben wird
content:
Teufelskreis


„Iran blockiert Straße von Hormus“, „Neue US-Angriffe auf Iran“, „Trump verkündet, Iran wolle verhandeln“, „Abkommen getroffen“, „Neue US-Angriffe auf Iran“, „Iran blockiert Straße von Hormus“. Seit fast einem halben Jahr wechseln sich diese Schlagzeilen ab und außer, dass die Preise an den Tankstellen mal um zehn bis zwanzig Cent sinken oder steigen, scheint sich kaum noch jemand wirklich dafür zu interessieren, was genau da eigentlich los ist oder wie es weiter geht mit dem Krieg zwischen den USA und dem Iran.


Das Problem ist, so richtig scheinen auch die führenden Köpfe des US-Imperiums keine Antwort auf diese Fragen zu haben. Dass sich die Schlagzeilen wie in einer Zwickmühle immer wieder wiederholen und es keinen Ausweg aus dem Teufelskreis dieses Krieges zu geben scheint, ist Ausdruck eines so gut wie nicht lösbaren Dilemmas, in den Trumps Angriff vom 28. Februar seine eigene Regierung manövriert hat. Trumps scheinbare Hoffnung, ein Angriff auf den Iran würde ähnlich schnell und erfolgreich verlaufen wie seine Kidnapping-Aktion in Venezuela, löste sich rasch in Luft auf, stattdessen sorgte der Enthauptungsschlag gegen den Iran nur dafür, dass das iranische Militär dezentralisiert die USA und ihre Verbündeten in der Region angriff wie nie zuvor und zum ersten Mal ihre mächtigste Waffe nutzten: die Blockade der Straße von Hormus.


Irans geographische Lage an der Meerenge und die Nähe zu den Golfstaaten erlauben es dem iranischen Militär ungeheuren Druck auf die gesamte Weltwirtschaft aufzubauen und damit vor allem die USA und ihre Vorherrschaft über diese Weltwirtschaft infrage zu stellen. Trotz aller Versuche der USA, die Blockade zu beenden, durch massive Zerstörung militärischer und ziviler Infrastruktur im Iran Druck aufzubauen und selbst eine Blockade der Straße von Hormus zu errichten, zeigte das durch Pakistan vermittelte „Memorandum of understanding“ Ende Juni, den einzigen Weg hin zu einer Deeskalation der Lage. Mit diesem einigten sich die USA und der Iran darauf, einen Weg hin zu einer diplomatischen Lösung finden zu wollen und dafür die gegenseitigen Angriffe aufeinander und auf die gesamte Weltwirtschaft einzustellen. Für einen Moment wirkte es, als könnte ein tatsächlicher Frieden absehbar sein, obwohl die USA damit quasi eine Niederlage eingestanden hätten und der Iran seine geopolitische Position im Vergleich zu vor dem Krieg hätte verbessern können. Doch schon zum Zeitpunkt dieser „Einigung“ war klar, dass es in den weiteren Verhandlungen vor allem darauf ankommen würde, wie sich der dritte entscheidende Spieler in diesem Konflikt verhalten würde: Israel.


Amerikanische vs. Israelische Interessen


Denn die offiziellen Kriegsziele der USA (zunächst Garantie, dass Iran keine nuklearen Waffen erlangt, später Öffnung der Straße von Hormus und wieder laufender Welthandel) waren trotz der militärischen Niederlage realistisch im Rahmen der Verhandlungen erreichbar. Schließlich hatte der Iran sich entgegen amerikanischer Propaganda auch schon zuvor an diplomatische Lösungen der nuklearen Frage gehalten und eine iranische Gebühr für die Öffnung der Straße von Hormus wäre für die USA zwar eine Niederlage, im Vergleich zur weiteren Blockade und damit dem drohenden Zusammenbruch der Weltwirtschaft aber doch eine kleine und hinnehmbare.


Doch für Israel stellt dieser Konflikt mit dem Iran einen existentiellen Kampf um die zionistische Zukunft im Nahen Osten dar. Die israelische Gesellschaft und Politik stecken in einer tiefen Krise (siehe:

Israel vor dem Abgrund – Bedeutet die Krise des Zionismus sein Ende?

), die vor allem durch den Kampf gegen „äußere“ Feinde und das Expansionsstreben sowohl in die palästinensischen Gebiete als auch in benachbarte Staaten wie Syrien und den Libanon aufgefangen wird. Doch die Zukunft Israels hängt vor allem davon ab, wie sich die Beziehung zu den USA weiter entwickeln wird. Israel ist auf die bedingungslose Unterstützung der größten Weltmacht angewiesen, um die eigene Vormachtstellung im Nahen Osten aufrechtzuerhalten und weiter auszubauen. Insgesamt verfolgt Israel dabei das Ziel, den Iran als einzigen verbliebenen regionalen Konkurrenten so nachhaltig wie möglich zu zerstören. Damit ist quasi jegliche weitere Eskalation der Lage im Interesse Israels. Nicht umsonst versucht die israelische Politik seit Jahrzehnten, die USA in einen Krieg mit dem Iran zu ziehen.


Der Libanon als Knackpunkt

author: The Case
title: Fake news και διαρροές για (και από) την περιβόητη έκθεση για τη Marfin
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Fake news και διαρροές για (και από) την περιβόητη έκθεση για τη Marfin


Από τη στιγμή που αποδείχθηκε ότι το ανώνυμο email (sic) που «έλαβαν» οι αρχές

κατονόμασε τον φυλακισμένο εκείνη την περίοδο Πολύκαρπο Γεωργιάδη

 ως έναν από τους εμπρηστές της Marfin, νέες διαρροές από την περιβόητη έκθεση της ΔΕΕ, σε φίλα προς την αστυνομία προσκείμενα δημοσιογραφικά παραμάγαζα, έρχονται να παραπληροφορήσουν ξανά.


Με ενθουσιασμό πληροφορηθήκαμε από το Mega, το Πρώτο Θέμα και άλλα μίντια ότι δόθηκε στη δημοσιότητα «απόσπασμα από βίντεο

που δείχνει ένα από τα άτομα να σπάει την τζαμαρία της τράπεζας

 πριν τη φονική επίθεση».


Στιγμιότυπο Mega [

πηγή

] [

αρχειοθετημένο

]


Στιγμιότυπο Πρώτο Θέμα [

πηγή

] [

αρχειοθετημένο

]


Κι όλα καλά ως εδώ, μόνο που η τζαμαρία η οποία φαίνεται στο στιγμιότυπο δεν είναι από τη Marfin αλλά από τη Συνεταιριστική Τράπεζα Χανίων στη Λεωφόρο Συγγρού.


Εύκολα μπορεί να διακρίνει κανείς, από τις φωτογραφίες της εποχής, ότι η μεν μπροστινή είσοδος της Marfin δεν είχε ποτέ κυκλική περιστρεφόμενη πόρτα, αλλά και ότι το πεζοδρόμιο ήταν διαφορετικό.


Η τράπεζα Marfin στη Σταδίου, Ιούλιος 2009 (Google Maps)


Αντίθετα, η πρόσοψη της Συνεταιριστικής Τράπεζας Χανίων στη Λεωφόρο Συγγρού φέρει, όπως διακρίνεται και πάλι σε φωτογραφίες της εποχής, τα ίδια χαρακτηριστικά με αυτά που διακρίνονται στο στιγμιότυπο που παρουσιάζουν οι επαγγελλόμενοι τους δημοσιογράφους.


Μάιος 2009


Η Συνεταιριστική Τράπεζα Χανίων, Λ. Συγγρού 68


Το ίδιο άλλωστε αναφέρει και η ίδια η έκθεση της ΔΕΕ, που καταγράφει το στιγμιότυπο ως «

ΤΡΑΠ ΧΑΝΙΩΝ 1-00-15.png

».


Από την έκθεση της ΔΕΕ


Τα παραπάνω εξηγούνται μόνο με έναν τρόπο.


Τα δημοσιογραφικά μαγαζιά δεν έχουν καταβάλει ούτε την στοιχειώδη προσπάθεια να καταλάβουν ή, έστω, να περάσουν ένα «δεύτερο μάτι» τις διαρροές που τους παραδίδονται από αστυνομικές πηγές. Είναι προφανές ότι τα «στοιχεία» τούς παραδίδονται ήδη σχολιασμένα από την πηγή τους και τα ΜΜΕ είναι παραπάνω από πρόθυμα να αυτοεξευτελιστούν, δημοσιεύοντας ως αλήθεια τον ισχυρισμό της αστυνομίας,

ακόμα κι αν διαψεύδεται από το ίδιο το «συγκλονιστικό» στοιχείο που τη συνοδεύει

.


Στο OmniaTV, παραμένοντας κατά της μαζικής παραγωγής παραπληροφόρησης, παρακολουθούμε στενά την υπόθεση «Μαρφίν 2.0». Περισσότερα, προσεχώς.

author: Wanessa Celina
title: Corrida eleitoral: partidos já podem oficializar candidaturas; vice de Flávio é incógnita
content:
O prazo para realização das convenções partidárias, que determinam a escolha final das candidaturas de federações e legendas para as

eleições de 2026

, começa nesta segunda-feira, 20 de julho, e segue até 5 de agosto. O PL realiza o encontro para oficializar a candidatura do senador

Flávio Bolsonaro

 à presidência da República no próximo sábado, 25, em sua sede de São Paulo.


Sem um nome de consenso para o cargo de vice-presidente no momento, Flávio Bolsonaro defende a formação de sua chapa com Daniella Marques

, que foi presidente da Caixa Econômica Federal na gestão de Jair Bolsonaro. O nome da economista, entretanto, não conta com o apoio do Partido Liberal. Marques é filiada ao Republicanos, partido que já chegou a negar apoio à pré-candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro.


Já no domingo, 26 de junho, é a vez do PSD apresentar o ex-governador de Goiás, Ronaldo Caiado, e o ex-prefeito de São Paulo e presidente do partido, Gilberto Kassab (PSD), como candidatos à presidente e vice-presidente, respectivamente. A convenção também ocorre em São Paulo. Um dos nomes confirmados na convenção nacional do PSD é o do governador de São Paulo e pré-candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas, que pretende apoiar apenas Kassab, já que apoia Flávio Bolsonaro para a presidência.


Romeu Zema, ex-governador de Minas Gerais, oficializa sua candidatura pelo partido Novo na próxima segunda-feira, 27, em Brasília.

 Para vice-presidente, Zema negocia com o empresário Geraldo Rufino (Podemos), ex-catador de reciclável, mas ainda não fez o anúncio oficialmente. Renan Santos será apresentado como candidato à presidência pelo partido Missão em 1.º de agosto. O seu vice já anunciado é o militar da reserva Aroldo Medina, do mesmo partido.


O presidente Lula deve oficializar sua candidatura à reeleição na convenção nacional do PT, em 2 de agosto, em São Paulo. Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) entra, mais uma vez, na sua chapa como vice-presidente.

Lula também deve aparecer para prestigiar a candidatura do seu ex-ministro da Fazenda, Fernando Haddad, para governador de São Paulo neste sábado, 25 de julho.


Dentro da agenda eleitoral, além das convenções partidárias, começa, nesta segunda-feira, 20, o período para que eleitores com deficiência ou mobilidade reduzida solicitem transferência para seções eleitorais adaptadas ou facilidades para votação em trânsito, que segue até o dia 20 de agosto. Além das pessoas com deficiência, pessoas que não estejam em seu domicílio eleitoral podem indicar o local onde pretendem votar e se desejam fazê-lo apenas no 1.º turno, apenas no 2.º, ou em ambos.


Estão na agenda das eleições de 2026, definida pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) entre os dias 20 a 26 de julho:


20 de julho:


Último dia para o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral publicar os limites de gastos de campanha estabelecidos em lei para cada cargo eletivo em disputa.


Data em que o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral divulgará, na internet, o quantitativo de eleitoras e eleitores aptos por município.


Data a partir da qual, até 30 de outubro de 2026, os processos eleitorais terão prioridade para a atuação do Ministério Público e dos juízos de todas as Justiças e instâncias.


24 de julho:


Último dia para a publicação do edital com os nomes das pessoas indicadas para compor as Juntas Eleitorais para o primeiro e eventual segundo turno de votação

.

author: Duda Sousa
title: De diversão a “renda extra” e “investimento”: como brasileiro mudou a percepção sobre bets
content:
Esta reportagem é parte de uma investigação especial da

Agência Pública

 financiada pelos nossos Aliados, sem nenhum dinheiro de bet. Apoie mais reportagens como essa

clicando aqui.


Todos os dias, cerca de 40 milhões de pessoas no Brasil depositam a sorte, e o dinheiro, em plataformas online de apostas, as bets. A estimativa é da empresa de infraestrutura de open finance Klavi e inclui o universo dos jogos de azar e das apostas esportivas. Se os apostadores diários formassem um estado brasileiro, ele seria o segundo mais populoso do país, atrás apenas de São Paulo. 


Ainda que números isoladamente não representem fielmente o cenário, eles ajudam a dar dimensão do mercado – e do desafio a ser enfrentado. A

Agência Pública

 cruzou pesquisas sobre o setor realizadas ao longo de quase uma década para evidenciar o quanto esse mercado mudou – e alterou a dinâmica do próprio país.


O levantamento mostra, por exemplo, que o contingente dos brasileiros que já realizaram algum tipo de aposta em plataformas digitais mais que dobrou em apenas três anos. A estimativa da Klavi é de que 74,29 milhões de brasileiros já tenham realizado apostas

 do tipo alguma vez, 34,8% da população. Em março de 2023, meses antes da regulamentação das casas de apostas online, aproximadamente 29,5 milhões de brasileiros já diziam ter realizado alguma aposta esportiva na internet, segundo o instituto Paraná Pesquisas, que indicava a atividade por 14,5% da população. 


Lúcio*, 26, fez sua primeira aposta há cinco anos, bem antes do governo federal decidir as regras para a legalidade das plataformas, em dezembro de 2023. Começou com R$ 50, por pura diversão em jogos de slots do tipo “tigrinho”. Como muitos, imaginava que bastava insistir um pouco para aumentar os ganhos. “Eu comecei por brincadeira mesmo. Colocava R$ 50, R$ 70 e ia dando certo, ia sacando. Só que aí comecei a querer apostar grande. Às vezes dava certo, às vezes não. Eu recebia meu pagamento, pagava as contas e o que sobrava ia para o jogo”, lembra.


As pequenas vitórias alimentavam a expectativa de compensação de prejuízos na próxima aposta. Aos poucos, a lógica deixou de ser ganhar dinheiro e passou a ser recuperar as perdas. E quando o salário já não era suficiente, a solução também foi a de muita gente. “Comecei a apelar para empréstimo. Peguei R$ 10 mil e perdi tudo. Hoje estou tentando arcar com uma dívida bem maior do que o valor que peguei, por causa dos juros”. 


Cinco anos antes da regulamentação, quando o Brasil autorizou as apostas esportivas de quota fixa, em 2018, ele sequer aparecia entre os 15 mercados com maior número de acessos a plataformas internacionais de apostas online

, segundo levantamento da Strategy&, da PwC. Em 2025, o país já ocupa a quinta posição no ranking mundial de acessos a sites de bets e movimenta aproximadamente R$ 360 bilhões, segundo estimativas da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC). 


Para o advogado especialista em direito esportivo e comunicação Andrei Kampff, o crescimento não pode ser explicado apenas pela legalização das apostas esportivas em 2018. “A Lei nº 13.756 abriu a porta ao legalizar as apostas de quota fixa, mas ela não explica, sozinha, esse crescimento. O mercado acelerou porque ficou, por anos, em uma zona de baixa regulação efetiva. Nós legalizamos uma atividade que sabidamente envolve riscos e esperamos mais de cinco anos para regulamentá-la e fiscalizá-la. Nesse período, os riscos aumentaram em vez de serem mitigados”.


Segundo Kampff, a expansão ocorreu em um contexto marcado pela popularização do Pix, pelo acesso massivo aos smartphones e pela presença crescente das plataformas no universo esportivo. “Houve segurança jurídica mínima para operar, enorme demanda digital, popularização do Pix, acesso pelo celular, marketing esportivo massivo e uma ausência inicial de fiscalização proporcional. Quando a Lei nº 14.790 entrou em vigor, o mercado já havia alcançado uma dimensão muito maior”.


Endividamento crônico


Além de encarar as apostas como uma fonte de renda extra ou imediata, o comportamento tradicional registrado por apostadores é o da tentativa de recuperar perdas.

O panorama mostrado pela Klavi mostra que três entre cada dez apostadores costumam solicitar crédito imediatamente antes de fazer uma aposta, comportamento que, segundo a empresa, eleva em 25% a chance de eles passarem a integrar a parcela da população brasileira que se encontra endividada.

author: winter oak
title: Through nature we can touch the divine
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


The spirituality of the ancient Celts, like that of most pre-modern peoples, was deeply rooted in human belonging to nature.


Jean Markale, in his very interesting 1985 book on druidism, explains that this was reflected in the fact that “before being conquered by the Romans or assimilated by the Greeks,

the Celts never built any temples

“. [1] They were rather the “men of the Tree” and officiated and taught in sacred clearings,

nemeta

, in the middle of the forests. [2]


“

Knowledge

 and

wood

 are symbolically placed in parallel”. [3] “The druids had a predilection for the forests and all the druids of Gaul met once a year in the forest of the Carnutes. In Britain, the druidic establishment on Ynys Môn (the island of Anglesey) was in a forest”. [4]


Describing a Celtic sanctuary near Marseilles, the Spanish-born Roman poet Lucan (39-65 AD) wrote: “The druids live in the deep woods (

nemora alta

) and withdraw into the uninhabited forests… They worship the gods in the woods without using temples”. [5]


As well as forests and islands, springs were also held sacred by the Celts (and many other peoples), says Markale – “there they found contact with the vibrant and fertile forces surging mysteriously from the centre of the earth”. [6]


Animals were obviously important in this spiritual

withness

 to nature – for instance, we learn that one of the roles of the Dagda, an important Celtic god described in the first article in this series, [7] was as “

master of the wild animals

 which he was charged with looking after in the forest”. [8]


And, as we saw in the second article, [9] there was a totemistic element to the Celts’ culture, with Markale noting that their myths often involve people “in animal form or bearing the names of animals”. [10]


Thus the legendary Irish hero Cú Chulainn, born Sétanta, got his new name (which means ‘Hound of Culann’) after killing Culann’s dog, then replacing him as this man’s protector – Markale sees this as an initiation rite into a clan whose emblem was the dog. [11]


In Irish and Scottish mythology, Diarmid Ua Dwibhne was closely linked to a wild boar and the same animal was also important in Wales and in Gaul. [12] Markale notes that most Gallic tribes seem to have gone into battle under the sign of the wild boar [13] – and I would add that similar images today adorn the vehicles of those who like to hunt

sangliers

 in rural France.


He continues: “Young Kulhwch [a cousin of King Arthur] was born in the middle of a herd of domestic pigs and young Pryderi, son of Rhiannon, was abducted at birth and then placed in a stable in which a foal had just been born”. [14]


“We also have to wonder why the Irish Art, son of Conn, which is to say “Bear, son of Dog’, has to have as his wife, having won her through braving terrible dangers, Coinchend Cennfada, in other words ‘Dogs’ heads’. The name of King Arthur, which is not of Latin origin as they would like us to believe, is derived from

artu

 or

arto

, ‘bear'”. [15]


As well as these symbolic namings, we also come across the shamanistic side of Celtic spirituality whose possible origins were mentioned in the last piece.


Says Markele: “We know that shamans, by their incantations and their ecstatic practices, can become animals, either by incorporating the spirit of the animal into themselves or by projecting themselves on to the animal. The transformation does not perhaps take place on the real

material

 level, but operates on a real psychological and mystical level”. [16]


“A good example of this is the story of Tuan mac Cairill (

pictured

), a highly interesting character from the Irish tradition. A witness to the five great invasions of Ireland, from the time of Partholon, he survived by changing forms. Initially a man (more precisely, a druid), he became a stag, a wild boar, a falcon and a salmon before turning back into a man”. [17]


Markale insists that this is not a question of a series of reincarnations, as some have suggested, but of successive metamorphoses of one being and one body: “Tuan mac Cairill is the image of primordial Man, still capable, as Mircea Eliade said of shamans, of reconstituting the golden age of humankind’s beginnings, when people and animals spoke the same language and did not kill each other”. [18]


He says his transformations “bear witness to the awareness that a being is not isolated in the universe and forms part of a whole …

author: CNT Catalunya-Balears
title: Firmado acuerdo de actualización de las tablas salariales del sector de la arqueología de Cataluña
content:
CNT Cataluña-Baleares informa de los recientes importantes acuerdos para el sector de la arqueología y la paleontología de Cataluña.


La CNT de Cataluña-Baleares ha participado en el acuerdo que pone fin a un largo agravio en el sector, junto con La Intersindical-CSC y la CGT de Cataluña.


Próximamente, se publicará el acuerdo que será de aplicación obligatoria en todas las empresas del sector. Todas las personas trabajadoras se beneficiarán, ya que las tablas salariales para los años 2026-27-28 y 29 recuperan de forma progresiva la pérdida producida en la última década. En algunos casos, los incrementos salariales podrán ser del 25% desde este 2026.


Además de esto, también se inicia el proceso de negociación de un nuevo Convenio colectivo, en el que participaremos en la mesa negociadora con el afán de obtener un nuevo marco que ponga fin a la precariedad y dignifique la profesión.


Desde la CNT nos congratulamos de los avances que se han tenido en este sector. Tenemos claro que nuestra actual fuerza viene gracias a la implantación de nuestro modelo sindical en algunas empresas. La huelga en Aixa Can Mançana, que ha superado los 300 días nos ha colocado como la principal fuerza sindical de la arqueología en Cataluña tanto en número de secciones como en número de personas afiliadas a nuestro sindicato y demuestra que la conflictividad crea mejores condiciones para la negociación colectiva.


Le invitamos a estudiar la publicación del acuerdo que se producirá en breve en el DOGC. A partir de su publicación este acuerdo entrará en vigor y tendrá una duración de 4 años, a contar desde el 1 de enero de 2026 y hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2029.


Arqueólogo, arqueóloga: ¡ha llegado el momento de organizarnos en un sindicato fuerte!


Si quieres que revisemos tu caso, puedes contactar con nosotros en el correo arqueologia@cnt.cat


¡Elige bien, elige CNT!

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo
